- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is rising, reduce overshoot by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming; add 3–5% buffer to prevent underestimation.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model should not overcorrect upward; cap forecast rise at 2–3% above prior peak.  
- After a sharp spike (e.g., +10%+ in 1–2 days), model tends to overreact; apply 1–2 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 2–3 days.  
- If sentiment is mixed (0.00–0.67) and price is volatile, model should not overfit short-term noise; use 3-day moving average to smooth forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently higher than forecast, adjust upward bias by 2–5% for next 5–7 days, especially if sentiment is neutral or positive.
